newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati protests election list.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati protests election list.

text.p: The ousted leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, urged the election commission on Wednesday to reject a provisional list of parliamentary candidates drawn up by her rival.
The commission on Monday released the provisional list of 2,293 candidates for the three political parties legally permitted to contest the May 29 general elections.
It includes the list of 744 candidates submitted by Megawati's government-backed rival, deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi, who ousted her at a rebel congress last June.
"We want the commission to reject the list because it has some problems," Roy Janis, a Megawati supporter, told reporters after presenting a protest letter to the commission on her behalf.
Interior Minister Yogie Memet was quoted by the official Antara news agency on Wednesday as dismissing Megawati's protest and said the PDI list from Surjadi was legal.
"It will not be withdrawn because it is legal," he said.
Janis said the list was illegal because Megawati was still suing Surjadi over her ouster at the June congress and had also challenged Surjadi's list of candidates in court.
Only the ruling Golkar, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the Christian-Nationalist PDI are allowed to contest the concurrent national, regional and municipal elections.
They will contest 425 seats in the 500-seat national assembly. The military, whose members do not vote, nominate the other 75 members.
The public has until February 18 to challenge the inclusion of candidates on the list. The official election campaign runs from April 29 to May 23, with the elections on May 29.
